newsitem.title: UK: Suezmax tanker rates in Med ease with Iraq flow.
newsitem.headline: Suezmax tanker rates in Med ease with Iraq flow.

text.p: Iraqi oil from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan began to flow in earnest on Thursday with some four vessels fixed, brokers said.

The tankers fixed include the Libyan flagged 155,000 dwt Elgurdabia which Trafigura fixed at W85 to Constanza, loading December 26, as well as the 142,000 dwt Marble chartered by Repsol to load December 24 which was said fixed at W83.75. The Oak was heard fixed by Shell at W80 to load 130,000 tonnes of Iraqi crude on December 30, with options to NWE or the Med.
A fourth ship, the Tito Tapias, was due to load 130,000 tonnes for Elf on December 21.
It was fixed to sail to Lavera, brokers said.

These vessels follow the Gole, the first ship to load Iraqi crude since the approval of the $2 billion U.N. oil for food deal, while two VLCCs have already left Mina al-Bakr in the Gulf for the U.S. and the Caribbean.
Rates for 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes were steady at lower levels, with three December fixtures seen at W80. This compared with rates 5-10 points higher last week.
From the Middle East to Japan, brokers said rates for 250,000 tonners were steady at the lower levels of W62.5. Several days ago, the rate was closer to W65.
In Asia-Pacific, brokers said fixtures for 80,000 tonners had firmed slightly to W145 from around W140 for Indonesia-Japan. "It's up a bit on tight tonnage," one said.

In the Med/Black Sea brokers noted a differential of about five points between new and old ships. One broker put cross-Med hops for old 80,000 tonners at W105, against W110 for modern vessels and W80 and W85 respectively for 130,000 tonners.
Rates for cross-UK/Cont routes were stronger amid a rash of fixtures, the highest of which was at W107.5. "There is a feeling that the Cont. is improving," a broker said.
